title: A description changed on the Part Library page writes Changed at history everywhere and renames the core
custom_preconds: Env https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com (S2 shop; locations Staging Heavy Duty and Staging Lethbridge). Current location Staging Heavy Duty. Logged in as Admin (or a default Parts Manager): Part Library & Inventory View, Create & Edit and Delete, and See Financial Data. API replays from Chrome DevTools against sv10647api.qa.shopview.com with header X-Location-ID = the current location. Data: QAPL-B1 (stocked at both locations; note its description as {old}); QAPL-C1 (Core Charge > 0, so it has a core; note its description as {c-old}). The core has no row of its own and its Part History has no on-screen link (S5-E3): read the core's part id from the DevTools responses while opening QAPL-C1.
custom_steps:
1. Parts > Part Library > open QAPL-B1 > pencil > change the Description to "{old} RN" ({new}) > Save.
  2. Parts > Inventory (Staging Heavy Duty) > QAPL-B1 row > history icon (Part History).
  3. Switch the location to Staging Lethbridge > Inventory > QAPL-B1 row > history icon.
  4. Switch back to Staging Heavy Duty > Part Library > open QAPL-C1 > pencil > change the Description to "{c-old} RN" ({c-new}) > Save.
  5. Open the core's Part History by its address /parts/history/{corePartId}, and replay GET /api/inventory/parts/{corePartId}.
  6. Restore both descriptions from the Part Library pencil ({old} on QAPL-B1, {c-old} on QAPL-C1) > Save each.
custom_expected:
1. While the field differs, "This also changes the description at 1 other location." shows under it. Save succeeds and the detail page shows {new}.
  2. The newest entry reads "Description updated | Original description: {old} | New description: {new}" with Staff, Date and Time, and no "Changed at".
  3. The row shows {new}. The newest entry reads "Description updated | Original description: {old} | New description: {new} | Changed at: Staging Heavy Duty".
  4. Saved; the detail page shows {c-new}.
  5. The core's newest entry is a "Description updated" entry written with the core's own description, ending "New description: Core for {c-new}"; the GET returns the name "Core for {c-new}".
  6. Both saves succeed and each part shows its original description again (the core follows: "Core for {c-old}").
